canonical_topic: Statistics as a shared vocabulary for traders
definition: Statistics is the branch of mathematics used to organize, analyze, and summarize data; traders rely on it as a common vocabulary so that numeric results can be communicated between people without ambiguity.
core_idea: Traders use standardized statistical terms (like volatility and correlation) so that descriptions of price behavior mean the same thing to everyone, rather than being open to individual interpretation.
key_points: Statistics serves traders primarily as a communication tool, not just an analytical one.
Terms such as volatility and correlation have fixed, agreed-upon meanings in trading contexts.
Statistical analysis has three main goals: summarizing time-series data, estimating confidence in that summary, and identifying relationships between phenomena.
relationships: Underpins the specific concepts of volatility and correlation used elsewhere in trading.
trading_implications: Precise statistical language lets traders convey results (e.g., 'the two prices are 40 percent correlated') unambiguously instead of vaguely.
caveats: Statistics are not facts — they are simplified descriptions that may or may not be true, and always carry an error bound.
